attributes.Details: On 6 February 2004, the remaining South Sydney City Council (SSCC) was amalgamated back into the City of Sydney. This created a new local government area (LGA) boundary for the City that has remained unchanged until the present day.

On 20 July 1842, the Sydney Corporation Act brought into being the Sydney Corporation, later known as the Council of the City of Sydney.

On 20 April 1870, the City of Sydney (known as the Municipal Council of Sydney until 1949) took over responsibility for the Moore Park area, initially by the device of making the Town Clerk the Trustee of Moore Park.
On 22 December 1908, the City of Sydney absorbed the Municipality of Camperdown.

On 1 January 1949, following the passing of the Local Government (Areas) Act 1948, the City of Sydney absorbed the surrounding municipalities of Alexandria, Darlington, Erskineville, The Glebe, Newtown, Paddington, Redfern and Waterloo.
